stories.headline: Houthis strike two Saudi oil tankers in the Red Sea and Brent crude tops $100

key_facts.fact: Yemen's Houthis said they attacked two Saudi oil tankers, the Encelia and the Layla, in the Red Sea on Thursday, July 23, causing fires aboard both vessels with no reported casualties.
key_facts.excerpt: The Houthis' SABA news agency said the rebels had struck two tankers, the Encelia and the Layla, in the Red Sea, leading to fires on both. There were no reports of casualties.

key_facts.fact: Brent crude futures rose $6.58, or 6.96%, to $100.65 a barrel, exceeding $100 for the first time since late May.
key_facts.excerpt: Brent futures rose $6.58 or 6.96 percent, to $100.65 a barrel, exceeding $100 for the first time since late May.

key_facts.fact: Saudi Arabia has rerouted more than 70% of its crude via pipeline to the Red Sea port of Yanbu since the near-total closure of the Strait of Hormuz in March; some 4.5 million barrels per day of exports from Yanbu are now under threat from the Houthi blockade.
key_facts.excerpt: As a result, Saudi Arabia moved to direct more than 70% of its crude shipments via pipeline to the port of Yanbu, on the kingdom's Red Sea coast. Some 4.5 million barrels per day of oil exports from Yanbu are now under threat by the Houthi blockade, affecting global oil prices.

key_facts.fact: The attacks were the first known strikes on Saudi ships since the Houthis declared a naval blockade on Monday against Saudi, Israeli and US-linked tankers in the Bab el-Mandeb strait.
key_facts.excerpt: On Monday, the Yemeni group declared a naval blockade on shipments from Saudi Arabia and said they would target Saudi, Israeli, and United States-linked tankers in the Bab el-Mandeb, which links the Red sea to the Indian Ocean.

key_facts.fact: President Donald Trump promised 'major military punishment' for Iran and its Houthi allies after the tanker strikes.
key_facts.excerpt: U.S. President Donald Trump promised "major military punishment" for Iran and its Houthi allies on Thursday after the Yemeni fighters struck two Saudi oil tankers in the Red Sea, extending the Middle East war to a second major shipping chokepoint.

key_facts.fact: Five tankers loaded with Saudi oil turned around in the Red Sea on Tuesday after the blockade declaration; four were bound for Bab el-Mandeb with millions of barrels for China and India and diverted toward the Suez Canal.
key_facts.excerpt: Five tankers loaded with Saudi oil turned round in the Red Sea on Tuesday, a day after the Houthi rebels announced a "maritime embargo" against Saudi Arabia. Four of the tankers, which were carrying millions of barrels of oil to markets including China and India, had been heading for the Bab Al Mandeb strait, but changed course towards the Suez Canal.

key_facts.fact: US pump prices have reached a national average of $4.09 per gallon amid the twin disruption at Hormuz and Bab el-Mandeb.
key_facts.excerpt: has sent prices soaring, including at the pump in the US reaching the national average of $4.09 per gallon (3.4 liter).

stories.headline: US hits Iran for a 13th straight night as Tehran strikes US bases in Kuwait, Bahrain and Iraq

key_facts.fact: US Central Command said it completed a 13th consecutive night of strikes against Iran at 9 p.m. ET Thursday, targeting Iranian military command centers, drone storage facilities, communication networks, coastal surveillance sites and maritime capabilities.
key_facts.excerpt: U.S. Central Command said it had completed a 13th straight night of strikes against Iran at 9 p.m. ET Thursday. CENTCOM said it targeted "Iranian military command centers, drone storage facilities, communication networks, coastal surveillance sites, and maritime capabilities."

key_facts.fact: Iran's Revolutionary Guard claimed it hit storage warehouses at a US base in Kuwait and a control tower of the US 5th Fleet in Bahrain, with explosions also reported near a base hosting US forces in northern Iraq.
key_facts.excerpt: Tehran launched new strikes, with the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps claiming to have hit storage warehouses at a U.S. base in Kuwait, and a control tower of the U.S. 5th Fleet in Bahrain. Explosions were reported near a military base hosting U.S. forces in northern Iraq.

key_facts.fact: Trump told Axios on Thursday he was weighing a 'massive attack' on Iran that would be 'bigger than ever before.'
key_facts.excerpt: Trump was weighing whether to launch a "massive attack" on the Islamic Republic that would be "bigger than ever before," he told Axios on Thursday.

key_facts.fact: Trump said on social media Thursday that frozen Iranian funds held by the US would pay for repairs to ships and cargo damaged in the conflict; Tehran called the move 'incendiary'.
key_facts.excerpt: On Thursday, US President Donald Trump said damages to ships and cargo in the Strait of Hormuz would be paid for by "Iranian Money that the United States has in its possession, and controls".

key_facts.fact: Air raid sirens sounded in Bahrain and Jordan and flights were suspended at Iraq's Erbil International Airport after a reported drone crash.
key_facts.excerpt: Iran later announced strikes on US-allied Kuwait, while sirens sounded in Bahrain and Jordan, and flights were suspended at a major Iraqi airport after a reported drone crash.

key_facts.fact: US strikes hit a Revolutionary Guard naval base in northern Iran, with blasts also reported on Qeshm Island in the Strait of Hormuz; Iranian state media said four people were killed and nine injured.
key_facts.excerpt: U.S. strikes hit a naval base for the Revolutionary Guard in the north of Iran, the Iranian semiofficial news outlets Fars and ISNA reported Friday morning. Blasts overnight were also reported on Iran's Qeshm Island... Iranian state media reported that four people had been killed and nine injured in the bombardment.

key_facts.fact: CENTCOM said it has redirected 12 commercial vessels and disabled one ship since resuming its naval blockade, and that more than 50,000 US service members are operating across the Middle East.
key_facts.excerpt: US Central Command (CENTCOM) said it has redirected 12 commercial vessels and disabled one ship since resuming its naval blockade... More than 50,000 US service members are operating across the Middle East.

key_facts.fact: The number of tankers crossing the Strait of Hormuz fell to just one on Thursday, the lowest level since May 7.
key_facts.excerpt: The number of tankers crossing the Strait of Hormuz fell to just one on Thursday, the lowest level since 7 May.

stories.headline: Nasdaq falls 2.15% as AI spending fears and $100 oil hit Wall Street; Tesla drops 14.5%

key_facts.fact: The Nasdaq Composite lost 553.21 points, or 2.15%, to 25,137.69; the S&P 500 fell 90.66 points, or 1.21%, to 7,408.30; and the Dow dropped 506.93 points, or 0.97%, to 51,711.65 on Thursday.
key_facts.excerpt: The Dow Jones Industrial Average fell 506.93 points, or 0.97%, to 51,711.65, the S&P 500 lost 90.66 points, or 1.21%, to 7,408.30 and the Nasdaq Composite lost 553.21 points, or 2.15%, to 25,137.69.

key_facts.fact: Tesla shares tumbled 14.5% after reporting negative free cash flow for the first time in more than two years, while Alphabet sank about 7% on higher spending plans and a cash burn.
key_facts.excerpt: Shares of Google's parent, Alphabet, sank 7%, making it the second-biggest drag on the benchmark index after it reported higher spending plans while it also burned cash... Its biggest drag was from Tesla, whose shares tumbled 14.5%, after it reported negative free cash flow in the second quarter for the first time in more than two years.

key_facts.fact: Alphabet and Tesla each grew quarterly revenue by at least 24% but together generated $43.8 billion in operating cash flow against $50.7 billion of capital spending, for combined free cash flow of negative $6.9 billion.
key_facts.excerpt: Together, they generated $43.8 billion in operating cash flow. Capital spending totaled $50.7 billion. Free cash flow was negative $6.9 billion. They invested $1.16 for every operating-cash dollar.

key_facts.fact: The selloff spread across Big Tech: Amazon fell nearly 5%, Meta almost 4% and Microsoft more than 2%, while the Philadelphia Semiconductor Index had already fallen more than 20% from its late-June peak.
key_facts.excerpt: Every major hyperscaler in the group traded sharply lower on Thursday. Amazon fell nearly 5%, Meta dropped almost 4%, and Microsoft slid more than 2%. The Philadelphia Semiconductor Index had already fallen more than 20% from its late-June peak before this week's results.

key_facts.fact: Soaring oil prices compounded the drop by reviving inflation worries and lifting bond yields.
key_facts.excerpt: Wall Street indexes closed lower on Thursday with Nasdaq sinking more than 2% as the latest earnings updates from large technology companies revived concerns about heavy AI spending, while soaring oil prices amped up inflation worries, lifting bond yields.

key_facts.fact: Tesla's automotive gross margin came in at 16.3% and its quarterly capital spending rose 142% to $5.8 billion, with Musk telling analysts 'this is a massive capex year'.
key_facts.excerpt: automotive gross margin came in at 16.3% against expectations of 18.04%. The cash burn traced directly to surging capex—$5.8 billion in the quarter, up 142%... Elon Musk told analysts: "This is a massive capex year, but I'm confident that all the things that we are investing in will yield incredible returns."

stories.headline: China fires water cannon at Philippine ships for a third time in a week near Scarborough Shoal

key_facts.fact: Chinese ships fired water cannon at Philippine vessels near Scarborough Shoal on Friday, including one carrying a CNN crew, in the third tense confrontation of the week in the contested waters.
key_facts.excerpt: Chinese ships fired water cannon at Philippine vessels, including one carrying a CNN crew, near a dangerous flashpoint in the South China Sea on Friday – the third tense confrontation this week in the contested waters.

key_facts.fact: The Philippine Coast Guard said its vessels were 'subjected to a series of water cannon attacks and dangerous maneuvers by China Coast Guard'; the Philippine ships eventually canceled their mission and returned to port, citing a developing typhoon.
key_facts.excerpt: The Philippine Coast Guard said its vessels had been "subjected to a series of water cannon attacks and dangerous maneuvers by China Coast Guard."... The Philippine ships eventually canceled their mission on Friday and headed back to port, citing a developing typhoon in the region.

key_facts.fact: In Thursday's incident, China Coast Guard vessel 3302 closed to 50 meters off the bow of BRP Datu Dumangsil and fired its water cannon for more than two minutes, scoring an indirect hit during a fuel-subsidy mission for Filipino fishermen.
key_facts.excerpt: "At approximately 5:54 a.m., CCG 3302 closed to merely 50 meters off the bow of BRP Datu Dumangsil, and at 6:29 a.m., it fired its water cannon at the vessel for more than two minutes, scoring an indirect hit," PCG spokesman Jay Tristan Tarriela said in a Facebook post.

key_facts.fact: The confrontations came as foreign ministers gathered in Manila for the 59th ASEAN Foreign Ministers' Meeting, where Chinese Foreign Minister Wang Yi warned Manila of 'bitter consequences of its own making' if it sought to provoke Beijing with outside support.
key_facts.excerpt: On the sidelines of a meeting of regional grouping ASEAN on Wednesday, the foreign ministers of both nations exchanged protests over the prior South China Sea encounter. China's Wang Yi warned Manila of "bitter consequences of its own making" if it sought to provoke Beijing with the support of outside powers.

key_facts.fact: Monday's incident at Second Thomas Shoal left a Philippine marine with a significant head injury after being struck with a baton by a China Coast Guard sailor, according to the Armed Forces of the Philippines.
key_facts.excerpt: The incident in question took place on Monday at Second Thomas Shoal in the Spratly Islands, during a confrontation between Philippine marines and personnel from the CCG. The Armed Forces of the Philippines (AFP) claimed that a Philippine marine sustained a significant head injury after being struck with a baton by a CCG sailor.

key_facts.fact: President Ferdinand Marcos Jr. met Chinese Ambassador Jing Quan on Tuesday to seek a 'reset' in relations, and on Thursday visited two Navy personnel injured at Second Thomas Shoal, awarding each the Order of Lapu-Lapu and 100,000 pesos.
key_facts.excerpt: "The President expressed his desire to ensure that these incidents do not recur and to reset Philippine-China relations toward better engagement"... On Thursday, Mr. Marcos also visited two Philippine Navy personnel injured during a confrontation with the CCG near Second Thomas Shoal and conferred on them the Order of Lapu-Lapu, along with P100,000 in financial assistance each.

key_facts.fact: The China Coast Guard said it tracked, monitored, blocked and expelled the Philippine vessels, which it accused of intruding into the waters of 'Huangyan Dao' despite repeated warnings.
key_facts.excerpt: "We urge the Philippines to immediately cease its infringing and provocative actions," China's Coast Guard said in a statement, while reaffirming sovereignty over the disputed shoal.

stories.headline: Zelensky pushes for three-way talks by autumn as Washington floats an air-only truce with Russia

key_facts.fact: Speaking at a joint press conference in Kyiv with Irish Prime Minister Micheál Martin on Thursday, Zelensky said new trilateral talks involving Ukraine, the US and Russia should take place by autumn.
key_facts.excerpt: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy on Thursday said new trilateral talks on a Ukraine settlement involving representatives from Kyiv, Moscow, and Washington should take place by autumn.

key_facts.fact: Zelensky said he received new proposals in a July 22 phone call with US envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner, which Washington will now take to Moscow.
key_facts.excerpt: The president said he received new proposals following a phone call on July 22 with US President Donald Trump's special envoys, Jared Kushner and Steve Witkoff. The American side will discuss these proposals with the Russian side.

key_facts.fact: Ukrainian and US officials told the Kyiv Independent that Washington believes the Kremlin may now be willing to accept at least a partial ceasefire in the air, with Ukraine running low on interceptors and Russia exposed to long-range Ukrainian strikes.
key_facts.excerpt: One U.S. official said the White House believes the Kremlin may now be more willing to accept at least a partial ceasefire in the air as Ukraine expands its strikes inside Russia... Ukraine is running low on interceptors, while Russia is exposed to long-range Ukrainian strikes.

key_facts.fact: Secretary of State Marco Rubio, after talks with Russian Foreign Minister Sergei Lavrov, said the US is committed to ending the 'senseless war' but acknowledged there is no quick path to a deal.
key_facts.excerpt: Secretary of State Marco Rubio said Thursday the Trump administration is poised to help end the "senseless war" in Ukraine but acknowledged there is no quick path to a deal, saying diplomacy will require sustained effort and new ideas.

key_facts.fact: Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov said on July 23 that Russia remains open to the negotiation process and hoped Witkoff and Kushner would travel to Moscow, but said there was no reason to talk of new momentum.
key_facts.excerpt: "Indeed, contacts [on Ukraine] are being made. It is always positive. But there is no need to talk about any new dynamics or new speeding up [of this process] right now," Peskov added.

key_facts.fact: Attacks on both sides killed at least eight people on Thursday — four in Ukraine and four in Russia and annexed Crimea — as the war entered its fifth year with the civilian toll at its highest since 2022.
key_facts.excerpt: Attacks by Russia and Ukraine have killed at least eight people, including a child, with four dead in Ukraine and another four in Russia and Moscow-annexed Crimea, officials on both sides say.

key_facts.fact: Ukraine's General Staff said overnight strikes on July 23 hit a Black Sea tanker carrying Russian crude and fuel for the army, a pontoon crossing near Novoekonomichne and a troop concentration in occupied Horlivka.
key_facts.excerpt: One of the targets was a tanker operating in the Black Sea. According to the Ukrainian military, the vessel was used to transport Russian crude oil, petroleum products, and fuel intended to support the country's army.

stories.headline: India cuts mobile internet in central Delhi and orders GitHub to pull Jack Dorsey's Bitchat

key_facts.fact: The Ministry of Home Affairs ordered mobile internet suspended across all technologies within a 1.5-km radius of Jantar Mantar from 4 p.m. to midnight on July 23, the sixth such order in a week.
key_facts.excerpt: Mobile data services have been directed to be cut within a radius of 1.5 kilometres around Jantar Mantar. A senior industry executive said that the internet suspension was initially issued to be valid till 4 pm on Thursday, but was later extended to midnight.

key_facts.fact: The Indian Cyber Crime Coordination Centre, under the Home Ministry, issued an order dated July 23 directing GitHub to disable three repositories hosting Bitchat within three hours, invoking Section 79(3)(b) of the IT Act and Rule 3(1)(d) of the IT Rules, 2021.
key_facts.excerpt: In an order dated July 23, shared by Dorsey on X and reviewed by Moneycontrol, I4C invoked Section 79(3)(b) of the Information Technology Act, along with Rule 3(1)(d) of the IT Rules, 2021, directing GitHub to disable access to three Bitchat repositories within three hours.

key_facts.fact: Bitchat's developer, Block CEO and former Twitter chief Jack Dorsey, posted on X on Friday: 'The Government of India does not like technologies like Bitchat and wants it taken down,' sharing a copy of the notice.
key_facts.excerpt: "The Government of India does not like technologies like Bitchat and wants it taken down," said the app's developer and former Twitter CEO Jack Dorsey on Friday in an X post, sharing a copy of the notice dated July 23.

key_facts.fact: Indian authorities said Bitchat's decentralized, registration-free Bluetooth mesh design thwarts lawful interception, as protesters turned to mesh-network tools to keep coordinating through the shutdowns.
key_facts.excerpt: Authorities say Bitchat's decentralized, registration-free design thwarts lawful interception and investigation, even as demonstrators rely on it and similar Bluetooth mesh apps to coordinate during exam scandal protests.

key_facts.fact: The protests, led by the satirical 'Cockroach Janta Party', began on June 20 and demand the resignation of Education Minister Dharmendra Pradhan over exam paper leaks affecting 2 million students.
key_facts.excerpt: The protests, led by the 'cockroach' movement, demand the resignation of Education Minister Dharmendra Pradhan due to widespread exam paper leaks affecting 2 million students. The digital blackout has hindered digital transactions in the area.

key_facts.fact: Delhi Metro closed stations near the protest site and all shops and restaurants in Connaught Place were ordered shut by 6:30 p.m. on July 23; the internet curbs hit small businesses that rely on UPI mobile payments.
key_facts.excerpt: Commuters' journeys and businesses were affected in Delhi as authorities blocked mobile internet services and shut metro stations in the nearby areas of Jantar Mantar... The internet curbs have hit small businesses particularly hard in a city where the bulk of payments are made through the Unified Payments Interface on mobile phones.

key_facts.fact: Mobile internet services were restored hours later on Thursday night after Delhi police gave assurances there would be no crackdown.
key_facts.excerpt: However, hours later, internet services were restored after Delhi police gave assurance for no-crackdown tonight.

stories.headline: US adds 12.5% forced-labor tariff on Brazil, lifting the total to 37.5%; Brasília heads to the WTO

key_facts.fact: The United States announced on Thursday, July 23, an additional 12.5% tariff on Brazilian goods over alleged forced labor in supply chains; the measure covers 60 countries and takes effect Friday.
key_facts.excerpt: In another protectionist move, the United States announced Thursday (23) an additional 12.5% tariff on Brazilian goods, arguing that the country has failed to address forced-labor practices in its supply chains. The measure applies to a total of 60 countries and takes effect this Friday.

key_facts.fact: For products already subject to the 25% Section 301 tariff that took effect on July 22, the new levy stacks on top, taking the combined rate to 37.5% by the Brazilian government's reading.
key_facts.excerpt: For Brazilian products already subject to the 25% tariff imposed under the Section 301 investigation, the new 12.5% levy will come on top of the existing duty... The Brazilian government expects the two rates to be cumulative, bringing the total tariff to 37.5%.

key_facts.fact: Lula's government called the tariff 'completely arbitrary and unjustified,' said it would immediately begin activating Brazil's Reciprocity Law and would take the dispute to the World Trade Organization's dispute-settlement mechanism.
key_facts.excerpt: It said it would immediately begin the [steps] needed to activate mechanisms under Brazil's Reciprocity Law, approved by Congress, and would bring the dispute before the World Trade Organization's international dispute-settlement mechanism.

key_facts.fact: Brazil's Ministry of Development, Industry, Trade and Services estimates the 25% tariff alone hits about 15% of Brazilian exports to the US, equivalent to $5.8 billion.
key_facts.excerpt: According to Brazil's Ministry of Development, Industry, Trade, and Services, the measure is expected to affect approximately 15 percent of Brazil's exports to the US – the equivalent to USD 5.8 billion in exports.

key_facts.fact: Lula said Brazil will stay at the negotiating table and challenged Washington to substantiate its allegations, arguing Brazil had submitted documents and proposals but 'never found reciprocity in the dialogue.'
key_facts.excerpt: He reiterated that Brazil will not abandon negotiations and called on Washington to provide evidence for the claims made against the country... the government had engaged in negotiations and submitted several documents to U.S. authorities but "never found reciprocity in the dialogue."

key_facts.fact: Lula said Brazil will seek new buyers rather than lament lost US sales: 'We are not going to sit around crying over the products we did not sell to [the United States] because we are going to look for other buyers.'
key_facts.excerpt: "We are not going to sit around crying over the products we did not sell to [the United States] because we are going to look for other buyers," he said.

key_facts.fact: Finance Minister Dario Durigan said Brazil's economic situation remains under control despite the US measures and the Middle East conflict.
key_facts.excerpt: Finance Minister Dario Durigan also rejected the additional tariff on Brazil. He said that despite the U.S. measures and the conflict in the Middle East, Brazil's economic situation remains under control.
